title: In-Situ TEM with Simultaneous Nanocalorimetry of the Crystallization of Phase Change Materials
content: Phase change materials (PCMs) are marginal glass formers that have applications in memristors and neuromorphic memory, because they may be rapidly switched between amorphous and crystalline phases, which have differentiating optoelectronic properties. Previous applications include rewritable DVDs, as the ‘recordable’ layer that could be written or erased by laser for memory storage. The leading PCM for that technology was Ge2Sb2Te5 (GST225), due to the rapid crystallization, appropriate crystallization temperature (∼148°C) for laser writing, and the high difference in optical properties between the amorphous and crystalline phase, allowing it to be ‘read’ after writing [1]. Similarly, for phase change memristor technology, the high difference in resistivity between the two phases and the rapid crystallization is needed, but at higher temperatures. One of the PCMs in this study, Ge7Sb93, is of interest due to its relevant crystallization temperature (∼275°C) in memristor applications [2].
